articles.title: Patient-Level Data for Drugs and Biological Products Submissions Containing Real-World Data and Real-World Evidence; Request for Information
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency), is announcing a request for information (RFI) from interested parties to share perspectives on patient-level data access related to the use of real-world evidence (RWE) in regulatory decision-making for drugs and biological product submissions. The purpose of this RFI is to solicit input from interested parties on innovative solutions to address the challenges in submitting patient-level data for real-world data (RWD) analyzed in clinical studies included in a marketing application. Interested parties may include regulated industry, health information technology (HIT) vendors, academic medical centers, electronic data capture vendors, patient advocates, and other interested parties.

articles.title: Early-Phase IND Protocol Recommendations for Solid Tumors; Draft Guidance for Industry; Availability

The purpose of this draft guidance is to provide recommendations to sponsors and clinical investigators developing early-phase trials, which include first-in- human (FIH) protocols or protocols for drugs and biologic products with limited human experience, submitted under an Investigational New Drug Application (IND) to the appropriate disease-specific division located within the Office of Oncologic Diseases (OOD) in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) and the Office of Clinical Evaluation (OCE) in the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER.) This draft guidance is specific to solid tumors and does not address protocols for investigational drugs intended to treat hematologic malignancies.

articles.title: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by the International Association of Color Manufacturers (IACM or petitioner), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of abandonment, to remove the authorized uses of methylene chloride, trichloroethylene, and ethylene dichloride from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin. The petitioner provided data demonstrating that these uses have been permanently abandoned. FDA is denying as moot the portion of the petition proposing that the color additive regulations be amended, on the basis of abandonment, to no longer authorize the use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. This request is moot because the authorization for this use has been removed, on the basis of the Delaney Clause, in response to a separate petition.

articles.title: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by Environmental Defense Fund et al. (petitioners), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of the Delaney Clause, to remove the authorized use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. The petitioners provided data demonstrating that this additive induces cancer in laboratory animals. We are denying the remaining petition requests to remove ethylene dichloride, methylene chloride, and trichloroethylene from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin, because any residue of the solvent would be an impurity in the color additive and such impurities are not subject to the Delaney Clause.

articles.title: Calendar Year 2027 Home Health Prospective Payment System (HH PPS) Rate Update; Requirements for the HH Quality Reporting Program and the Expanded HH Value-Based Purchasing Model; Medicare Provider Enrollment, Durable Medical Equipment (DME), and DME, Prosthetics, Orthotics, and Supplies (DMEPOS) Policies
articles.summary: This final rule sets forth routine updates to the Medicare home health payment rates in accordance with existing statutory and regulatory requirements. In addition, this final rule discusses the behavior adjustments and finalizes a temporary behavior adjustment. It also finalizes the recalibrated case-mix weights and updated functional impairment levels; comorbidity subgroups; and low-utilization payment adjustment (LUPA) thresholds for CY 2027. Additionally, this final rule discusses and responds to comments on the provision of home health palliative care services and includes a summary of comments received on the request for information (RFI) on a home health specific wage index included in the proposed rule. This rule also finalizes changes to the Home Health Quality Reporting Program (HH QRP) and summarizes potential initiatives to improve alignment between the HH QRP and expanded Home Health Value- Based Purchasing (HHVBP) Model. Lastly, the rule clarifies the application of the DMEPOS face-to- face encounter requirements for the replacement of DMEPOS items; makes changes to the provider and supplier enrollment requirements; makes changes to implement a DME benefit expansion for infusion pumps and drugs; and discusses collection of information requirement changes regarding the DMEPOS Competitive Bidding Program (CBP) country of origin.

articles.title: Medicare Program: Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment Systems; and Quality Reporting Programs; including the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Program; Request for Information on Strengthening the Standardization and Comparability of Hospital Price Transparency (HPT) Data; Prior Authorization; Accrediting Organization (AO) Deeming for Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA); and Notices of Closure of Teaching Hospitals and Opportunities To Apply for Available Slots
articles.summary: This final rule with comment period revises the Medicare Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and the Medicare Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) payment system for calendar year 2027 based on our continuing experience with these systems. We also describe the changes to the amounts and factors used to determine the payment rates for Medicare services paid under the OPPS and those paid under the ASC payment systems. In addition, this final rule with comment period updates and refines the requirements for the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and the Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program. There are no changes to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program. We finalized the expansion of the prior authorization requirement to include additional Botulinum Toxin Injection services. We also finalized implementation of certain provisions of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, for off-campus outpatient departments of a provider. In addition, this final rule with comment period announces notices of closure of teaching hospitals and opportunities to apply for available slots. Additionally, we finalized the policy that hospital accrediting organizations (AOs) with deeming authority may assess compliance with certain Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20 during accreditation and reaccreditation surveys.

articles.title: Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products; Guidance for Industry; Availability
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a final guidance titled "Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products." The guidance document provides recommendations to help assure the potency of human cellular therapy or gene therapy (CGT) products at all stages of the product lifecycle. FDA is recommending a comprehensive approach to potency assurance of CGT products that is grounded in quality risk management. For investigational products, we describe how to progressively implement a strategy for potency assurance during product development and provide additional considerations to help assure the potency of products that are undergoing rapid clinical development. For licensed products, we describe requirements for potency assurance, including testing required for lot release assays. The guidance announced in this notice finalizes the draft guidance of the same title issued on December 28, 2023.

articles.title: Recommendations for Reducing the Risk of Transfusion-Transmitted Hepatitis B Virus; Guidance for Industry; Availability
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a final guidance titled "Recommendations for Reducing the Risk of Transfusion-Transmitted Hepatitis B Virus." The guidance document provides blood establishments that collect blood and blood components, including Source Plasma, with FDA's recommendations for testing blood and blood components for hepatitis B virus (HBV) to reduce the risk of transfusion-transmitted HBV. The recommendations contained in the guidance apply to the collection of Whole Blood and blood components, including Source Plasma. The guidance announced in this notice finalizes the draft guidance titled "Recommendations for Testing Blood Donations for Hepatitis B Surface Antigen" (July 2025 Draft Guidance). The guidance also supersedes the documents titled "Recommendations for the Management of Donors and Units that are Initially Reactive for Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg)" (December 1987 Memorandum), "FDA Recommendations Concerning Testing for Antibody to Hepatitis B Core Antigen (Anti-HBc)" (September 1991 Memorandum), "Adequate and Appropriate Donor Screening Tests for Hepatitis B; Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) Assays Used to Test Donors of Whole Blood and Blood Components, Including Source Plasma and Source Leukocytes" (November 2007 Final Guidance), "Requalification Method for Reentry of Blood Donors Deferred Because of Reactive Test Results for Antibody to Hepatitis B Core Antigen (Anti-HBc)" (May 2010 Final Guidance), "Requalification Method for Reentry of Donors Who Test Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) Positive Following a Recent Vaccination against Hepatitis B Virus Infection" (November 2011 Final Guidance), and "Use of Nucleic Acid Tests on Pooled and Individual Samples from Donors of Whole Blood and Blood Components, Including Source Plasma, to Reduce the Risk of Transmission of Hepatitis B Virus" (October 2012 Final Guidance). The guidance supersedes the recommendations specific to HBV in "Recommendations for the Quarantine and Disposition of Units from Prior Collections from Donors with Repeatedly Reactive Screening Tests for Hepatitis B Virus (HBV), Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) and Human T- Lymphotropic Virus Type I (HTLV- I)" (July 1996 Memorandum).

articles.summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is requesting that an information collection request revision for the Review Choice Demonstration or Home Health Services (CMS-10599/0938- 1311) processed under the emergency clearance process associated with the implementing regulations of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA). Public harm is reasonably likely to occur if normal, non- emergency clearance procedures are followed. The approval of this data collection process is essential to ensure that the Review Choice Demonstration (RCD) for Home Health (HH) Services is expanded to California within the specified timeframe. A delay in the expansion means an extended time the public will be harmed through the continuation of significant fraud found in the traditional Medicare home health benefit in California through the waste of taxpayer money, a loss of funds from the Medicare Trust Funds that could have been used for truly needed care, paying for care that is never delivered, and beneficiaries potentially receiving non-medically necessary care. Under the PRA, federal agencies are required to publish notice in the Federal Register concerning each proposed ICR. Interested persons are invited to send comments regarding our burden estimates or any other aspect of this ICR including the necessity and utility of the proposed ICR for the proper performance of the agency's functions, the accuracy of the estimated burden, ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected and the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology to minimize the information collection burden.

articles.title: Infant Formula Nutrient Requirements
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) proposes to amend the regulations on nutrient specifications and labeling for infant formula as part of its phased, comprehensive review of infant formula nutrients. This action, if finalized, would amend the minimum and/or maximum levels of four required nutrients, change the unit of measure for certain nutrients, change the permitted source to meet one of the nutrient requirements, and amend the content of the required labeling. This action also includes a comprehensive assessment of four additional nutrients for which we conclude that the current required levels remain appropriate and reflect the best available scientific evidence on infant nutritional requirements and safe intake levels.

articles.title: Essential Drug Delivery Performance Characteristics for Devices Intended To Deliver Drugs and Biological Products; Revised Draft Guidance for Industry; Availability
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a revised draft guidance for industry entitled "Essential Drug Delivery Performance Characteristics for Devices Intended to Deliver Drugs and Biological Products." This revised draft guidance revises and replaces the draft guidance entitled "Essential Drug Delivery Outputs Intended to Deliver Drugs and Biological Products" announced in the Federal Register on July 1, 2024 (89 FR 54470). In accordance with its mission of protecting, promoting, and advancing public health, this guidance addresses key aspects of drug delivery performance information for devices, and combination products that include device constituent parts, intended for delivery of a human drug, including a biological product (herein referred to as drug delivery devices). This guidance provides recommendations for development and organization of device drug-delivery performance information and data to improve the consistency of this information in applications and to facilitate transparency and predictability in development and regulatory review. The guidance is intended to facilitate and streamline development and lifecycle management of drug delivery devices.

articles.title: Medical Devices; Anesthesiology Devices; Classification of the Over-the-Counter Device To Assess Risk of Sleep Apnea
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is classifying the over-the-counter device to assess risk of sleep apnea into class II (special controls). The special controls that apply to the device type are identified in this order and will be part of the codified language for classification of the over-the-counter device to assess risk of sleep apnea. We are taking this action because we have determined that classifying the device into class II will provide a reasonable assurance of the safety and effectiveness of the device. We believe this action will also enhance patients' access to beneficial innovative devices, in part by reducing regulatory burdens.

articles.title: Privacy Act of 1974; Matching Program
articles.summary: In accordance with subsection (e)(12) of the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), is providing notice of a computer matching program between CMS and the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA). The purpose of the matching program is to identify beneficiaries enrolled in both Medicare and VHA health care and to identify medical claims for which both agencies made payment for the same health care services. Under this agreement, the VHA will provide CMS with a finder file on a recurring basis, of all Veteran beneficiaries enrolled in VHA health care that CMS will use to identify dually enrolled beneficiaries. CMS and VHA will use the results of the matching program to recover duplicate payments, improve payment accuracy, and identify potential fraud, waste, and abuse.

Despite having a legal work permit, issued by DHS itself, the same agency took her away in the middle of the night.
